candidates.core_provocation: In the near future, a stranger asks a woman to store one of his memories for twenty-four hours because his memory is about to be legally erased. When she opens it, she finds a vivid memory of herself killing someone tomorrow—and the stranger insists she must help make sure it does not happen.
candidates.why_interesting: The reader must keep asking whether the memory is a prediction, a trap, or an event the woman has somehow already forgotten.

candidates.core_provocation: People can buy and sell recorded memories, and a man purchases a cheap memory from a stranger to learn a lost skill. Instead, he receives the stranger’s eyewitness memory of a crime, making him the only person who can identify the killer—and the killer knows exactly what he has seen.
candidates.why_interesting: A simple commercial transaction turns a private memory into dangerous evidence, creating immediate suspense between two people who have never met.

candidates.core_provocation: After a new treatment allows people to delete one painful memory, a stranger approaches a woman and claims she is the only person who still remembers their shared night. She has no memory of him, but he knows details about her life that only the missing memory could explain.
candidates.why_interesting: The mystery is both personal and urgent: she must decide whether recovering the memory will reveal a forgotten crime, a lost love, or a reason to fear the stranger.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The first idea creates the strongest immediate hook: a stranger’s memory gives the protagonist a concrete future crime and a limited time to act. It also uses the near-future technology to create uncertainty without requiring a large cast or complicated world-building.
